summary:
AstroZone is an IoT-based Astronaut Health Monitoring System designed to improve astronaut safety by combining health monitoring, cabin environmental information, and NASA space weather data on a single web-based platform.

The system uses an ESP32 connected to MAX30100, AD8232 ECG, DS18B20, and MPU6050 sensors to collect health, temperature, and movement readings. The data is transmitted to a backend for validation, processing, and storage, then displayed through a web dashboard.

The platform includes user authentication, health monitoring, NASA space weather information, alerts, and historical data visualization. It helps mission control teams observe important parameters, identify unusual changes, and make informed decisions.

AstroZone's main advantage is its centralized approach to monitoring multiple data sources. However, further testing is required to establish sensor accuracy, system response time, reliability, and clinical validity. Blood pressure measurement and cabin temperature monitoring also require clearer technical implementation.

Future improvements include AI-based anomaly detection, predictive health analysis, radiation dose tracking, and advanced wearable sensors.
details:
AstroZone – Protecting Life Beyond Earth

AstroZone is an IoT-based Astronaut Health Monitoring System developed to support astronaut safety by integrating health monitoring, environmental information, and NASA space weather data into a centralized web platform.

The system uses an ESP32 microcontroller connected to MAX30100, AD8232 ECG, DS18B20, and MPU6050 sensors to collect health, temperature, and movement readings. These readings are transmitted through Wi-Fi to a Python FastAPI backend, where they are validated, processed, and stored in MongoDB Atlas. A React-based dashboard presents health measurements, historical trends, space weather information, and alerts to mission control teams.

The project uses React.js, JavaScript, Python, FastAPI, MongoDB, Arduino C++, REST APIs, and WebSockets. NASA research and space weather sources provide additional mission-related information.

AstroZone's innovation lies in combining IoT hardware, centralized health monitoring, space weather intelligence, and AI-based analysis within a single platform. It aims to reduce information fragmentation, improve awareness of potential risks, and support faster decision-making.

The team considered data accuracy, reliability, security, real-time communication, scalability, and user experience. Future improvements include predictive health analysis, AI-based anomaly detection, radiation dose tracking, and advanced wearable sensors.
